typedef struct TU_ATTR_PACKED {
  uint8_t  bLength            ; ///< Size of this descriptor in bytes
  uint8_t  bDescriptorType    ; ///< INTERFACE Descriptor Type

  uint8_t  bInterfaceNumber   ; ///< Number of this interface. Zero-based value identifying the index in the array of concurrent interfaces supported by this configuration.
  uint8_t  bAlternateSetting  ; ///< Value used to select this alternate setting for the interface identified in the prior field
  uint8_t  bNumEndpoints      ; ///< Number of endpoints used by this interface (excluding endpoint zero). If this value is zero, this interface only uses the Default Control Pipe.
  uint8_t  bInterfaceClass    ; ///< Class code (assigned by the USB-IF). \li A value of zero is reserved for future standardization. \li If this field is set to FFH, the interface class is vendor-specific. \li All other values are reserved for assignment by the USB-IF.
  uint8_t  bInterfaceSubClass ; ///< Subclass code (assigned by the USB-IF). \n These codes are qualified by the value of the bInterfaceClass field. \li If the bInterfaceClass field is reset to zero, this field must also be reset to zero. \li If the bInterfaceClass field is not set to FFH, all values are reserved for assignment by the USB-IF.
  uint8_t  bInterfaceProtocol ; ///< Protocol code (assigned by the USB). \n These codes are qualified by the value of the bInterfaceClass and the bInterfaceSubClass fields. If an interface supports class-specific requests, this code identifies the protocols that the device uses as defined by the specification of the device class. \li If this field is reset to zero, the device does not use a class-specific protocol on this interface. \li If this field is set to FFH, the device uses a vendor-specific protocol for this interface.
  uint8_t  iInterface         ; ///< Index of string descriptor describing this interface
} tusb_desc_interface_t;

functions.name: tu_edpt_dir
functions.signature: TU_ATTR_ALWAYS_INLINE static inline tusb_dir_t tu_edpt_dir(uint8_t addr)
functions.description: Returns the USB endpoint direction (TUSB_DIR_IN or TUSB_DIR_OUT) extracted from a USB endpoint address. Intended for quickly decoding bit7 of a standard endpoint address value.
requirements: addr must be a valid USB endpoint address where bit7 indicates direction (1=IN, 0=OUT).
Behavior is defined only for standard USB endpoint address encoding; other bits are ignored aside from bit7.

functions.name: tu_edpt_number
functions.signature: TU_ATTR_ALWAYS_INLINE static inline uint8_t tu_edpt_number(uint8_t addr)
functions.description: Extracts and returns the endpoint number (0–15) from a USB endpoint address by masking with 0x0F. Useful when decoding descriptors or endpoint handles.
requirements: addr must be a valid USB endpoint address encoded per USB spec (endpoint number in bits 0..3).
Returned value is in the range [0, 15].

functions.name: tu_edpt_addr
functions.signature: TU_ATTR_ALWAYS_INLINE static inline uint8_t tu_edpt_addr(uint8_t num, uint8_t dir)
functions.description: Constructs a USB endpoint address from an endpoint number and a direction. Sets bit7 for IN endpoints when dir == TUSB_DIR_IN; otherwise returns OUT (bit7 clear).
requirements: num must be in the range [0, 15] (fits TUSB_EPNUM_MASK = 0x0F).
dir must be either TUSB_DIR_IN or TUSB_DIR_OUT.
The caller is responsible for ensuring the (num, dir) pair corresponds to an actually-configured endpoint in the device.

functions.name: tu_edpt_packet_size
functions.signature: TU_ATTR_ALWAYS_INLINE static inline uint16_t tu_edpt_packet_size(tusb_desc_endpoint_t const* desc_ep)
functions.description: Returns the wMaxPacketSize (11-bit max packet field) from a USB endpoint descriptor, converting from little-endian and masking to 0x7FF. Useful for determining the maximum payload per transaction.
requirements: desc_ep must be non-null and point to a valid, initialized tusb_desc_endpoint_t populated from a USB descriptor (wMaxPacketSize in little endian).
Only the lower 11 bits of wMaxPacketSize are returned; high-speed additional transaction bits (bits 11..12) are masked out.

functions.name: tu_edpt_type_str
functions.signature: TU_ATTR_ALWAYS_INLINE static inline const char *tu_edpt_type_str(tusb_xfer_type_t t)
functions.description: Returns a constant string describing a transfer type: "control", "isochronous", "bulk", or "interrupt". Provided for debugging/logging builds (guarded by CFG_TUSB_DEBUG).
requirements: Available only when compiled with CFG_TUSB_DEBUG enabled; otherwise this function may not be present.

t must be one of the defined tusb_xfer_type_t values (TUSB_XFER_CONTROL=0, TUSB_XFER_ISOCHRONOUS=1, TUSB_XFER_BULK=2, TUSB_XFER_INTERRUPT=3); passing values outside 0..3 leads to out-of-bounds array access.

functions.name: tu_print_mem
functions.signature: void tu_print_mem(void const *buf, uint32_t count, uint8_t indent);
functions.description: Dumps a memory block to the debug output. The function prints the contents of the buffer pointed to by buf for count bytes, typically formatted as hex with an indent/prefix level specified by indent. Intended for debugging and only available when CFG_TUSB_DEBUG is enabled. Exact output format is not shown in this header and may vary by implementation.
requirements: Only available/defined when CFG_TUSB_DEBUG is non-zero.
buf must point to a readable memory region of at least count bytes when count > 0.
indent is used to control indentation/prefix spacing; valid range/semantics are not documented here (unknown).
Produces output via the configured debug print backend (tu_printf); ensure that backend is available/initialized if required by the platform.

functions.name: tu_printf
functions.signature: int tu_printf(const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Debug-print function-like macro that routes to either a user-provided printf-compatible function (CFG_TUSB_DEBUG_PRINTF) or the standard printf. Used throughout debugging helpers to print formatted messages. Only defined when CFG_TUSB_DEBUG is enabled.
requirements: Only available/defined when CFG_TUSB_DEBUG is non-zero.
If CFG_TUSB_DEBUG_PRINTF is defined, it must declare a function with signature int CFG_TUSB_DEBUG_PRINTF(const char *format, ...).
When routed to standard printf, the format string and arguments must follow printf rules (e.g., matching types for format specifiers).
The format pointer must be a valid, readable null-terminated C string.
Variadic arguments must correspond exactly to the format specifiers to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: tu_print_buf
functions.signature: static inline void tu_print_buf(uint8_t const* buf, uint32_t bufsize);
functions.description: Prints a buffer as a sequence of hexadecimal byte values to the debug output, followed by CRLF. Implemented inline here using tu_printf("%02X ", buf[i]). Intended for quick inspection of raw byte buffers during debugging.
requirements: Only available/defined when CFG_TUSB_DEBUG is non-zero (relies on tu_printf).
buf must point to a readable memory region of at least bufsize bytes when bufsize > 0.
Safe to call with bufsize == 0 (prints just a newline).
Output depends on the availability of a working tu_printf backend.

functions.name: tu_lookup_find
functions.signature: static inline const char* tu_lookup_find(tu_lookup_table_t const* p_table, uint32_t key);
functions.description: Looks up a key in a lookup table and returns the associated C string. If the key is not found, returns a pointer to a static buffer containing the key formatted as a hexadecimal string (e.g., "0x1234ABCD"). Intended for turning numeric codes into human-readable strings for logs.
requirements: Only available/defined when CFG_TUSB_DEBUG is non-zero.
p_table must be a valid pointer to a tu_lookup_table_t with items pointing to an array of at least p_table->count elements.
Each items[i].data must be a valid, null-terminated C string when matched.
Not thread-safe for the not-found path: the returned fallback string resides in a shared static buffer and will be overwritten by subsequent calls.
Callers must copy the returned string if it needs to be retained across subsequent calls or used concurrently across threads.
If snprintf fails (returns <= 0), the function returns a pointer to a static buffer with an empty string (per implementation).

functions.name: tusb_time_millis_api
functions.signature: extern uint32_t tusb_time_millis_api(void);
functions.description: Application-provided function that returns the current time in milliseconds. Used by TinyUSB on ports/configurations without an RTOS.
requirements: Must be implemented by the application (no default implementation provided).
Should return a monotonically increasing millisecond counter (wraparound behavior is implementation-defined/unknown).
Must be callable at the times TinyUSB uses it (e.g., from task or ISR context) — specific context requirements are not specified/unknown.

functions.name: tusb_time_delay_ms_api
functions.signature: extern void tusb_time_delay_ms_api(uint32_t ms);
functions.description: Application-provided millisecond delay/sleep. Default behavior is to base delays on tusb_time_millis_api() when no RTOS is present.
requirements: Must be implemented by the application if required by the port/configuration.
Parameter ms is a delay in milliseconds; all uint32_t values are accepted (0 is a no-op).
Blocking behavior, accuracy, and ISR safety are implementation-defined/unknown.

functions.name: tusb_app_dcache_flush
functions.signature: extern void tusb_app_dcache_flush(uintptr_t addr, uint32_t data_size);
functions.description: Application hook to flush (clean) the CPU data cache for a memory region so that writes are visible to DMA/peripherals.
requirements: Must be implemented by the application when cache maintenance is needed on the platform.
addr is the start address of the region; data_size is the size in bytes.
addr must reference a valid memory region at least data_size bytes long; alignment and granularity requirements are platform-specific/unknown.

functions.name: tusb_app_dcache_invalidate
functions.signature: extern void tusb_app_dcache_invalidate(uintptr_t addr, uint32_t data_size);
functions.description: Application hook to invalidate the CPU data cache for a memory region so that subsequent CPU reads fetch updated data from memory/peripherals.
requirements: Must be implemented by the application when cache maintenance is needed on the platform.
addr is the start address of the region; data_size is the size in bytes.
addr must reference a valid memory region at least data_size bytes long; alignment and granularity requirements are platform-specific/unknown.

functions.name: tusb_app_virt_to_phys
functions.signature: extern void* tusb_app_virt_to_phys(void *virt_addr);
functions.description: Optional application hook to translate a virtual address to a physical address for DMA/peripheral use.
requirements: Implementation is optional (platform-dependent).
virt_addr may be NULL or any pointer; returned mapping and NULL-on-failure behavior are implementation-defined/unknown.

functions.name: tusb_app_phys_to_virt
functions.signature: extern void* tusb_app_phys_to_virt(void *phys_addr);
functions.description: Optional application hook to translate a physical address back to a CPU-usable virtual address.
requirements: Implementation is optional (platform-dependent).
phys_addr may be any pointer-like value; returned mapping and NULL-on-failure behavior are implementation-defined/unknown.

functions.name: tu_memset_s
functions.signature: TU_ATTR_ALWAYS_INLINE static inline int tu_memset_s(void *dest, size_t destsz, int ch, size_t count);
functions.description: C11-like safe memset. Writes count bytes of value ch into dest with runtime parameter validation. Returns 0 on success, -1 on invalid parameters.
requirements: dest must be non-NULL unless count == 0.
If count == 0, function returns 0 and performs no writes.
count must be <= destsz, otherwise returns -1 without writing.
Caller must provide a valid writable buffer of at least count bytes at dest.

functions.name: tu_memcpy_s
functions.signature: TU_ATTR_ALWAYS_INLINE static inline int tu_memcpy_s(void *dest, size_t destsz, const void *src, size_t count);
functions.description: C11-like safe memcpy. Copies count bytes from src to dest with runtime parameter validation. Returns 0 on success, -1 on invalid parameters.
requirements: dest must be non-NULL unless count == 0.
src must be non-NULL unless count == 0.
If count == 0, function returns 0 and performs no copy.
count must be <= destsz, otherwise returns -1 without copying.
dest must be a valid writable buffer of at least count bytes; src must be a valid readable buffer of at least count bytes.
Behavior for overlapping regions is the same as memcpy (undefined); do not pass overlapping buffers.

functions.name: tu_mem_is_zero
functions.signature: TU_ATTR_ALWAYS_INLINE static inline bool tu_mem_is_zero(const void *buffer, size_t size);
functions.description: Checks whether all size bytes in buffer are zero.
requirements: buffer must be a valid readable region of at least size bytes.
size may be 0 (returns true).

functions.name: tu_mem_is_ff
functions.signature: TU_ATTR_ALWAYS_INLINE static inline bool tu_mem_is_ff(const void *buffer, size_t size);
functions.description: Checks whether all size bytes in buffer are 0xFF.
requirements: buffer must be a valid readable region of at least size bytes.
size may be 0 (returns true).

requirements: Must be invoked by the MCU’s USB IRQ handler when a USB device interrupt occurs for the specified rhport.

functions.name: tud_speed_get
functions.signature: tusb_speed_t tud_speed_get(void);
functions.description: Get the current USB bus speed negotiated with the host.

functions.name: tud_connected
functions.signature: bool tud_connected(void);
functions.description: Check whether the device is connected to a host (may not yet be configured). True after coming out of bus reset and receiving the first data from the host.

functions.name: tud_mounted
functions.signature: bool tud_mounted(void);
functions.description: Check whether the device is connected and configured (mounted) by the host.

functions.name: tud_suspended
functions.signature: bool tud_suspended(void);
functions.description: Check whether the USB bus is suspended.

functions.name: tud_ready
functions.signature: bool tud_ready(void);
functions.description: Check whether the device is ready for data transfer, i.e., mounted and not suspended. Inline convenience combining tud_mounted() and tud_suspended().

functions.name: tud_remote_wakeup
functions.signature: bool tud_remote_wakeup(void);
functions.description: Initiate a remote wakeup to the host if the bus is suspended and the host has enabled remote wakeup for the device.
requirements: May only succeed when the device is suspended.
Remote wakeup must have been enabled by the host.

functions.name: tud_disconnect
functions.signature: bool tud_disconnect(void);
functions.description: Enable the D+/D- pull-up resistor disconnect to simulate cable unplug (disable pull-up). Returns false on unsupported MCUs.

functions.name: tud_connect
functions.signature: bool tud_connect(void);
functions.description: Disable the D+/D- pull-up resistor disconnect to simulate cable plug-in (enable pull-up). Returns false on unsupported MCUs.

functions.name: tud_sof_cb_enable
functions.signature: void tud_sof_cb_enable(bool en);
functions.description: Enable or disable Start-of-Frame (SOF) callback support, which invokes tud_sof_cb() each (micro)frame when enabled.
requirements: en controls whether SOF callbacks are generated.

functions.name: tud_control_xfer
functions.signature: bool tud_control_xfer(uint8_t rhport, tusb_control_request_t const * request, void* buffer, uint16_t len);
functions.description: Carry out the data and status stages of a control transfer on the given port using the provided setup request and data buffer. If len is 0, only a status stage is sent; if len exceeds wLength, the transfer is truncated.
requirements: request must point to a valid tusb_control_request_t corresponding to the current control transfer.
If len == 0, the function behaves as a status-only transfer.
If len > wLength in the setup request, data will be truncated to wLength.
buffer must be suitably sized for len bytes when a data stage is present.

functions.name: tud_control_status
functions.signature: bool tud_control_status(uint8_t rhport, tusb_control_request_t const * request);
functions.description: Send a zero-length status packet to complete a control transfer on the given port for the specified setup request.
requirements: request must point to the tusb_control_request_t associated with the control transfer being completed.

functions.name: tud_descriptor_device_cb
functions.signature: uint8_t const * tud_descriptor_device_cb(void);
functions.description: Application callback invoked on GET DEVICE DESCRIPTOR. Return a pointer to the device descriptor. The memory must persist long enough for the transfer to complete.
requirements: Must return a valid pointer to a USB device descriptor buffer.
The descriptor contents must remain valid until the control transfer completes.

functions.name: tud_descriptor_configuration_cb
functions.signature: uint8_t const * tud_descriptor_configuration_cb(uint8_t index);
functions.description: Application callback invoked on GET CONFIGURATION DESCRIPTOR. Return a pointer to the configuration descriptor for the given index. Memory must persist for the duration of the transfer.
requirements: index selects which configuration descriptor to return.
Must return a valid pointer to a configuration descriptor buffer.
The descriptor contents must remain valid until the control transfer completes.

functions.name: tud_descriptor_string_cb
functions.signature: uint16_t const* tud_descriptor_string_cb(uint8_t index, uint16_t langid);
functions.description: Application callback invoked on GET STRING DESCRIPTOR. Return a pointer to the string descriptor for the given index and language ID. Memory must persist for the transfer duration.
requirements: index selects which string descriptor to return.
langid is the USB language ID requested by the host.
Must return a valid pointer to a UTF-16LE string descriptor buffer.
The descriptor contents must remain valid until the control transfer completes.

functions.name: tud_descriptor_bos_cb
functions.signature: uint8_t const * tud_descriptor_bos_cb(void);
functions.description: Application callback invoked on GET BOS DESCRIPTOR. Return a pointer to the BOS descriptor.
requirements: Must return a valid pointer to a BOS descriptor buffer that remains valid for the duration of the control transfer.

functions.name: tud_descriptor_device_qualifier_cb
functions.signature: uint8_t const* tud_descriptor_device_qualifier_cb(void);
functions.description: Application callback invoked on GET DEVICE QUALIFIER DESCRIPTOR. Return a pointer to the descriptor that describes the device if it operated at the opposite speed. If the device is not high-speed capable, the request should be stalled (by returning a condition per implementation).
requirements: Must return a valid pointer to a device qualifier descriptor buffer that remains valid for the transfer duration, or stall the request if not high-speed capable.

functions.name: tud_descriptor_other_speed_configuration_cb
functions.signature: uint8_t const* tud_descriptor_other_speed_configuration_cb(uint8_t index);
functions.description: Application callback invoked on GET OTHER SPEED CONFIGURATION DESCRIPTOR. Return a pointer to the configuration descriptor at the other speed (FS vs HS) for the given index. Memory must persist for the transfer duration.
requirements: index selects which other-speed configuration descriptor to return.
Returned buffer must remain valid until the control transfer completes.

functions.name: tud_mount_cb
functions.signature: void tud_mount_cb(void);
functions.description: Application callback invoked when the device is mounted (configured) by the host.

functions.name: tud_umount_cb
functions.signature: void tud_umount_cb(void);
functions.description: Application callback invoked when the device is unmounted by the host.

functions.name: tud_suspend_cb
functions.signature: void tud_suspend_cb(bool remote_wakeup_en);
functions.description: Application callback invoked when the USB bus is suspended. Within 7 ms, the device must draw an average current less than 2.5 mA from the bus. The parameter indicates if remote wakeup is enabled by the host.
requirements: On suspend, within 7 ms the device must reduce average current draw to less than 2.5 mA.
remote_wakeup_en indicates whether remote wakeup is permitted by the host.

functions.name: tud_resume_cb
functions.signature: void tud_resume_cb(void);
functions.description: Application callback invoked when the USB bus is resumed from suspend.

functions.name: tud_event_hook_cb
functions.signature: void tud_event_hook_cb(uint8_t rhport, uint32_t eventid, bool in_isr);
functions.description: Application callback invoked when a new USB event occurs that needs processing by tud_task()/tud_task_ext(). Provides the port, event ID, and whether the event occurred in ISR context.

functions.name: tud_sof_cb
functions.signature: void tud_sof_cb(uint32_t frame_count);
functions.description: Application callback invoked on each new USB (micro)frame when SOF callback support is enabled. frame_count is the running frame counter.

functions.name: tud_vendor_control_xfer_cb
functions.signature: bool tud_vendor_control_xfer_cb(uint8_t rhport, uint8_t stage, tusb_control_request_t const * request);
functions.description: Application callback invoked for control requests of VENDOR type. Handle the request at the given control transfer stage and return status.
requirements: stage indicates the control transfer stage and must be handled per TinyUSB’s control flow.
request must point to the received vendor-specific setup packet.

functions.name: tud_int_handler
functions.signature: void tud_int_handler(uint8_t rhport);
functions.description: Alias macro to dcd_int_handler; serves as the TinyUSB device interrupt handler entry for the specified root hub port. Should be hooked to the MCU’s USB IRQ vector to service device interrupts.
requirements: Must be called from the MCU’s USB interrupt context for the corresponding rhport.
Symbol is a macro alias; the underlying implementation is dcd_int_handler.

functions.name: tuh_enum_descriptor_device_cb
functions.signature: void tuh_enum_descriptor_device_cb(uint8_t daddr, const tusb_desc_device_t* desc_device);
functions.description: Application callback invoked by the TinyUSB host stack when the device descriptor has been retrieved during enumeration. The device is not ready for communication yet; the application may inspect/copy the descriptor.
requirements: This function is implemented by the application (it is a weak/extern callback).
Must not assume the device is configured or ready; only descriptor data is valid.
desc_device must be treated as read-only and only valid during the callback invocation unless copied.

functions.name: tuh_enum_descriptor_configuration_cb
functions.signature: bool tuh_enum_descriptor_configuration_cb(uint8_t daddr, uint8_t cfg_index, const tusb_desc_configuration_t* desc_config);
functions.description: Application callback invoked when a configuration descriptor is obtained during enumeration. For multi-configuration devices, return true to proceed with this configuration, or false to skip it (note: skipping may not be fully implemented yet). The device is not yet ready for communication.
requirements: This function is implemented by the application.
Must return a boolean to indicate whether to proceed with the provided configuration.
Must not assume the device is configured or ready; only descriptor data is valid.
desc_config is read-only and only valid during the callback invocation unless copied.

functions.name: tuh_mount_cb
functions.signature: void tuh_mount_cb(uint8_t daddr);
functions.description: Application callback invoked when a device has been successfully configured (mounted). Use this to start class drivers or application I/O.
requirements: This function is implemented by the application.
May be called from task or ISR context depending on stack configuration; write code accordingly (re-entrancy/latency sensitive).
daddr is the device address assigned by the host stack.

functions.name: tuh_umount_cb
functions.signature: void tuh_umount_cb(uint8_t daddr);
functions.description: Application callback invoked when a device is unmounted (detached). Use to cleanup state and stop I/O for the device.
requirements: This function is implemented by the application.
Must not access device endpoints after unmount.
daddr is the address that was assigned to the device before detach.

functions.name: tuh_event_hook_cb
functions.signature: void tuh_event_hook_cb(uint8_t rhport, uint32_t eventid, bool in_isr);
functions.description: Application event hook invoked when the host stack posts a new USB event that will be processed by tuh_task()/tuh_task_ext(). Can be used for diagnostics or waking a main loop/RTOS.
requirements: This function is implemented by the application.
May be invoked from ISR context when in_isr is true; avoid blocking operations in that case.
rhport is the root hub port index; eventid identifies the internal event (opaque to the app unless known).

functions.name: tuh_configure
functions.signature: bool tuh_configure(uint8_t rhport, uint32_t cfg_id, const void* cfg_param);
functions.description: Configures host stack behavior with dynamic/port-specific parameters before initialization. The meaning of cfg_param depends on cfg_id (e.g., MAX3421 settings, or platform-specific configurations).
requirements: Must be called before initializing the host stack on the target rhport (i.e., before tuh_rhport_init/tuh_init).
cfg_id must be a valid configuration ID recognized by the build (e.g., TUH_CFGID_RPI_PIO_USB_CONFIGURATION, TUH_CFGID_MAX3421).
cfg_param must point to the structure required by cfg_id (e.g., tuh_configure_max3421_t for TUH_CFGID_MAX3421).
Returns false on invalid parameters.

functions.name: tuh_rhport_init
functions.signature: bool tuh_rhport_init(uint8_t rhport, const tusb_rhport_init_t* rh_init);
functions.description: Initializes the TinyUSB host stack on a specific root hub port using the provided role/speed configuration.
requirements: Must be called before using the host API on the specified rhport.
rh_init must not be NULL and must specify role=TUSB_ROLE_HOST and a valid speed.
Returns false if initialization fails.

functions.name: tuh_init
functions.signature: static inline bool tuh_init(uint8_t rhport);
functions.description: Deprecated inline convenience wrapper that initializes the host stack on a root hub port using default speed based on TUH_OPT_HIGH_SPEED. Prefer tuh_rhport_init (or tusb_init) with explicit tusb_rhport_init_t.
requirements: Should be called before any other host operations on rhport.
Subject to deprecation; migrate to tuh_rhport_init/tusb_init.
Returns false if initialization fails.

functions.name: tuh_deinit
functions.signature: bool tuh_deinit(uint8_t rhport);
functions.description: Deinitializes the host stack on the specified root hub port, releasing resources and halting bus activity.
requirements: rhport must refer to an initialized host port.
All outstanding transfers on that port should be completed/aborted before deinit to avoid side effects.
Returns false on invalid rhport or if deinitialization fails.

functions.name: tuh_inited
functions.signature: bool tuh_inited(void);
functions.description: Reports whether the host stack is initialized on any root hub port.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time to check global init state.

functions.name: tuh_task_ext
functions.signature: void tuh_task_ext(uint32_t timeout_ms, bool in_isr);
functions.description: Processes pending host events and timeouts. Extended form of tuh_task() with control over wait time and ISR context flag.
requirements: Should be called regularly from a main loop or RTOS task to drive the host stack.
timeout_ms is the wait time in milliseconds: 0 = no wait, 0xFFFFFFFF = wait forever.
If called from ISR, pass in_isr=true; in ISR context, must not block for long (platform restrictions apply).

functions.name: tuh_task
functions.signature: static inline void tuh_task(void);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for tuh_task_ext with an infinite wait (UINT32_MAX) and in_isr=false. Drives host stack processing in a polling loop.
requirements: Call regularly from main/RTOS context (non-ISR).
Blocks until an event or timeout according to platform behavior.

functions.name: tuh_task_event_ready
functions.signature: bool tuh_task_event_ready(void);
functions.description: Returns whether there are pending USB host events that need processing by tuh_task()/tuh_task_ext().
requirements: Can be polled from the main loop to decide when to call tuh_task().

functions.name: hcd_int_handler
functions.signature: void hcd_int_handler(uint8_t rhport, bool in_isr);
functions.description: Low-level Host Controller Driver interrupt handler entry point. TinyUSB provides a macro alias tuh_int_handler(...) that forwards to this with optional in_isr argument.
requirements: Intended to be called from the MCU's USB ISR or equivalent interrupt context.
rhport selects the root hub port raising the interrupt.
in_isr should reflect ISR context (true when called from ISR).

functions.name: tuh_rhport_is_active
functions.signature: bool tuh_rhport_is_active(uint8_t rhport);
functions.description: Checks whether the specified root hub port is initialized and active as a USB host.
requirements: rhport must be within the supported port index range.

functions.name: tuh_rhport_reset_bus
functions.signature: bool tuh_rhport_reset_bus(uint8_t rhport, bool active);
functions.description: Asserts or de-asserts the USB bus reset signal on the specified root hub port. USB spec suggests holding reset for 10–50 ms.
requirements: rhport must refer to an initialized host port.
Call with active=true to assert reset, then active=false to release after the required duration.
Returns false on invalid port or if operation not supported.

functions.name: tuh_vid_pid_get
functions.signature: bool tuh_vid_pid_get(uint8_t daddr, uint16_t* vid, uint16_t* pid);
functions.description: Retrieves the cached Vendor ID and Product ID of a device at the given address.
requirements: daddr must refer to a known device.
vid and pid pointers must be non-NULL and writable.
Returns false if the device is unknown or parameters are invalid.

functions.name: tuh_descriptor_get_device_local
functions.signature: bool tuh_descriptor_get_device_local(uint8_t daddr, tusb_desc_device_t* desc_device);
functions.description: Fetches the locally cached device descriptor for an already enumerated device.
requirements: daddr must refer to an enumerated device.
desc_device must be non-NULL and writable.
Returns false if the descriptor is not available or parameters are invalid.

functions.name: tuh_speed_get
functions.signature: tusb_speed_t tuh_speed_get(uint8_t daddr);
functions.description: Returns the operating USB speed of the specified device (e.g., full, high).
requirements: daddr must refer to a known device address.

functions.name: tuh_mounted
functions.signature: bool tuh_mounted(uint8_t daddr);
functions.description: Checks whether the specified device is connected and configured (mounted).
requirements: daddr must refer to a device address; returns false if not mounted.

functions.name: tuh_connected
functions.signature: bool tuh_connected(uint8_t daddr);
functions.description: Checks whether the device has successfully completed at least one transfer (i.e., is connected). Device may not yet be addressed/configured/mounted.
requirements: daddr must refer to a potential/known device; returns false if no successful transfer yet.

functions.name: tuh_suspended
functions.signature: static inline bool tuh_suspended(uint8_t daddr);
functions.description: Checks whether the device is suspended. Currently returns false (suspend/resume not implemented in host).
requirements: No special requirements; do not rely on suspension status until implemented.
Parameter daddr is unused in current implementation.

functions.name: tuh_ready
functions.signature: static inline bool tuh_ready(uint8_t daddr);
functions.description: Convenience check that returns true if the device is mounted and not suspended, indicating it is ready for I/O.
requirements: Relies on tuh_mounted(daddr) and tuh_suspended(daddr).
daddr must refer to a device address.

functions.name: tuh_bus_info_get
functions.signature: bool tuh_bus_info_get(uint8_t daddr, tuh_bus_info_t* bus_info);
functions.description: Retrieves bus information for a device, including root hub port, hub address/port (if behind a hub), and negotiated speed.
requirements: daddr must refer to a known device.
bus_info must be non-NULL and writable.
Returns false if the device is unknown or parameters are invalid.

functions.name: tuh_control_xfer
functions.signature: bool tuh_control_xfer(tuh_xfer_t* xfer);
functions.description: Submits a control transfer to a device. If a completion callback is provided, the call is asynchronous; otherwise it blocks until completion.
requirements: xfer must be non-NULL and properly initialized.
For control transfers, xfer->setup must point to a valid setup packet; xfer->buffer points to data stage buffer as applicable.
If xfer->complete_cb == NULL (blocking), xfer->user_data should be a pointer to an xfer_result_t variable to receive the result (per Transfer API convention).
Returns false if parameters are invalid or a control transfer is already in progress for the device.

functions.name: tuh_edpt_xfer
functions.signature: bool tuh_edpt_xfer(tuh_xfer_t* xfer);
functions.description: Submits a bulk/interrupt transfer to a non-control endpoint. Asynchronous if a completion callback is provided; otherwise blocks until complete.
requirements: xfer must be non-NULL and properly initialized (daddr, ep_addr, buffer, expected length in union buflen).
Endpoint must be opened before transfer (see tuh_edpt_open).
If xfer->complete_cb == NULL (blocking), xfer->user_data should be a pointer to an xfer_result_t variable to receive the result.
Returns false on invalid parameters or if submission fails.

functions.name: tuh_edpt_open
functions.signature: bool tuh_edpt_open(uint8_t daddr, const tusb_desc_endpoint_t* desc_ep);
functions.description: Opens a non-control endpoint described by the endpoint descriptor for the specified device.
requirements: daddr must refer to a known device.
desc_ep must be non-NULL and describe a non-control endpoint supported by the device configuration.
Returns false if parameters are invalid or the endpoint cannot be opened.

functions.name: tuh_edpt_close
functions.signature: bool tuh_edpt_close(uint8_t daddr, uint8_t ep_addr);
functions.description: Closes a previously opened non-control endpoint and aborts any pending transfers on it.
requirements: daddr must refer to a known device; ep_addr is the endpoint address (with direction bit).
Transfers on the endpoint will be aborted; callers should handle aborted completions.
Returns false if the endpoint is not open or parameters are invalid.

functions.name: tuh_edpt_abort_xfer
functions.signature: bool tuh_edpt_abort_xfer(uint8_t daddr, uint8_t ep_addr);
functions.description: Attempts to abort a queued transfer on the specified endpoint. Only transfers that have not started can be aborted.
requirements: daddr must refer to a known device; ep_addr is the endpoint address.
Only queued (not yet started) transfers can be aborted.
Returns true if a queued transfer was aborted; false if no transfer was aborted.

functions.name: tuh_address_set
functions.signature: bool tuh_address_set(uint8_t daddr, uint8_t new_addr, tuh_xfer_cb_t complete_cb, uintptr_t user_data);
functions.description: Performs a standard SET_ADDRESS control transfer to assign a new USB address to a device.
requirements: daddr is the current temporary address; new_addr is the address to set.
Follows Transfer API semantics: asynchronous if complete_cb != NULL; if complete_cb == NULL (blocking), user_data should point to an xfer_result_t variable.
Returns false on invalid parameters or if a control transfer is already in progress.

functions.name: tuh_configuration_set
functions.signature: bool tuh_configuration_set(uint8_t daddr, uint8_t config_num, tuh_xfer_cb_t complete_cb, uintptr_t user_data);
functions.description: Issues a SET_CONFIGURATION control transfer. A config_num of 0 unconfigures the device. Note: config_num is 1-based (descriptor index + 1).
requirements: daddr must refer to the target device.
config_num must be a valid configuration number for the device (0 to unconfigure).
True on success; false if there is an on-going control transfer or incorrect parameters.
If complete_cb == NULL (blocking), user_data should point to an xfer_result_t variable.

functions.name: tuh_interface_set
functions.signature: bool tuh_interface_set(uint8_t daddr, uint8_t itf_num, uint8_t itf_alt, tuh_xfer_cb_t complete_cb, uintptr_t user_data);
functions.description: Issues a SET_INTERFACE control transfer to select an alternate setting for an interface.
requirements: daddr must refer to the target device.
itf_num must be a valid interface number; itf_alt must be a supported alternate setting.
True on success; false if there is an on-going control transfer or incorrect parameters.
If complete_cb == NULL (blocking), user_data should point to an xfer_result_t variable.

functions.name: tuh_descriptor_get
functions.signature: bool tuh_descriptor_get(uint8_t daddr, uint8_t type, uint8_t index, void* buffer, uint16_t len, tuh_xfer_cb_t complete_cb, uintptr_t user_data);
functions.description: Requests a descriptor (by type and index) via a control transfer and copies it into buffer. Asynchronous if a completion callback is provided; otherwise the call blocks.
requirements: daddr must refer to the target device.
buffer must be non-NULL with capacity at least len bytes.
True on success; false if there is an on-going control transfer or incorrect parameters.
If complete_cb == NULL (blocking), user_data should point to an xfer_result_t variable.

functions.name: tuh_descriptor_get_device
functions.signature: bool tuh_descriptor_get_device(uint8_t daddr, void* buffer, uint16_t len, tuh_xfer_cb_t complete_cb, uintptr_t user_data);
functions.description: Fetches the device descriptor via control transfer into buffer.
requirements: daddr must refer to the target device.
buffer must be non-NULL and at least len bytes.
True on success; false if there is an on-going control transfer or incorrect parameters.
If complete_cb == NULL (blocking), user_data should point to an xfer_result_t variable.

functions.name: tuh_descriptor_get_configuration
functions.signature: bool tuh_descriptor_get_configuration(uint8_t daddr, uint8_t index, void* buffer, uint16_t len, tuh_xfer_cb_t complete_cb, uintptr_t user_data);
functions.description: Fetches the configuration descriptor (by index) via control transfer into buffer.
requirements: daddr must refer to the target device; index selects the configuration (0-based).
buffer must be non-NULL and at least len bytes.
True on success; false if there is an on-going control transfer or incorrect parameters.
If complete_cb == NULL (blocking), user_data should point to an xfer_result_t variable.

functions.name: tuh_descriptor_get_hid_report
functions.signature: bool tuh_descriptor_get_hid_report(uint8_t daddr, uint8_t itf_num, uint8_t desc_type, uint8_t index, void* buffer, uint16_t len, tuh_xfer_cb_t complete_cb, uintptr_t user_data);
functions.description: Fetches an HID report-related descriptor (e.g., report descriptor) for the given interface via control transfer into buffer.
requirements: daddr must refer to the target device; itf_num is the HID interface number.
desc_type must be a valid HID descriptor type for the request; index selects the descriptor/ID as applicable.
buffer must be non-NULL and at least len bytes.
True on success; false if there is an on-going control transfer or incorrect parameters.
If complete_cb == NULL (blocking), user_data should point to an xfer_result_t variable.

functions.name: tuh_descriptor_get_string
functions.signature: bool tuh_descriptor_get_string(uint8_t daddr, uint8_t index, uint16_t language_id, void* buffer, uint16_t len, tuh_xfer_cb_t complete_cb, uintptr_t user_data);
functions.description: Fetches a USB string descriptor (by index and language ID) into buffer via control transfer. If complete_cb is NULL, the call blocks.
requirements: daddr must refer to the target device; index is the string index.
language_id is the language (0 for default/langid table when index==0).
buffer must be non-NULL and at least len bytes.
Explicitly documented: blocking when complete_cb is NULL; in that case, user_data must contain an xfer_result_t variable (pointer).
True on success; false if there is an on-going control transfer or incorrect parameters.

functions.name: tuh_descriptor_get_string_langid
functions.signature: static inline bool tuh_descriptor_get_string_langid(uint8_t daddr, void* buffer, uint16_t len, tuh_xfer_cb_t complete_cb, uintptr_t user_data);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to fetch the language ID (string index 0, language_id 0) string descriptor into buffer.
requirements: Same requirements as tuh_descriptor_get_string, with index=0 and language_id=0.
buffer must be non-NULL and at least len bytes.
If complete_cb == NULL (blocking), user_data must point to an xfer_result_t variable.

functions.name: tuh_descriptor_get_manufacturer_string
functions.signature: bool tuh_descriptor_get_manufacturer_string(uint8_t daddr, uint16_t language_id, void* buffer, uint16_t len, tuh_xfer_cb_t complete_cb, uintptr_t user_data);
functions.description: Fetches the manufacturer USB string descriptor for the given language into buffer.
requirements: daddr must refer to the target device.
buffer must be non-NULL and at least len bytes.
True on success; false if there is an on-going control transfer or incorrect parameters.
If complete_cb == NULL (blocking), user_data should point to an xfer_result_t variable.

functions.name: tuh_descriptor_get_product_string
functions.signature: bool tuh_descriptor_get_product_string(uint8_t daddr, uint16_t language_id, void* buffer, uint16_t len, tuh_xfer_cb_t complete_cb, uintptr_t user_data);
functions.description: Fetches the product USB string descriptor for the given language into buffer.
requirements: daddr must refer to the target device.
buffer must be non-NULL and at least len bytes.
True on success; false if there is an on-going control transfer or incorrect parameters.
If complete_cb == NULL (blocking), user_data should point to an xfer_result_t variable.

functions.name: tuh_descriptor_get_serial_string
functions.signature: bool tuh_descriptor_get_serial_string(uint8_t daddr, uint16_t language_id, void* buffer, uint16_t len, tuh_xfer_cb_t complete_cb, uintptr_t user_data);

functions.name: tuc_init

functions.description: Initializes the TinyUSB Type-C stack for the specified root hub port. Call this once per port before using other Type-C/PD APIs. The port_type selects the Type-C port configuration/role (details not documented here). Returns true on successful initialization, false otherwise.
requirements: Must be called before any other tuc_* API that operates on the same rhport (e.g., tuc_task_ext, tuc_msg_request).
rhport must refer to a valid, configured root hub port index for the platform.

functions.name: tuc_task_ext
functions.signature: void tuc_task_ext(uint32_t timeout_ms, bool in_isr);
functions.description: Processes Type-C/PD stack tasks and events. This extended task API allows specifying a wait timeout and whether the call occurs in an interrupt context. Intended to be called regularly from the main loop or RTOS task; may also be invoked from an ISR when in_isr is set accordingly. timeout_ms semantics: 0 = no wait, 0xFFFFFFFF (UINT32_MAX) = wait forever.
requirements: Should be called periodically in the main loop or an RTOS task to drive the Type-C/PD stack.
If called from an ISR, in_isr must be set to true; otherwise set to false.
timeout_ms controls internal waiting/blocking; use 0 for non-blocking polling and UINT32_MAX for indefinite wait.
Do not pass UINT32_MAX when calling from an ISR (indefinite wait is not ISR-safe).
The corresponding rhport(s) should have been initialized with tuc_init prior to relying on task processing for that port.

functions.name: tuc_task
functions.signature: static inline void tuc_task(void);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for tuc_task_ext that runs the Type-C/PD task with an infinite wait and non-ISR semantics (equivalent to tuc_task_ext(UINT32_MAX, false)). Intended for use in a main loop or RTOS task.
requirements: Must not be called from an ISR (it uses infinite wait and in_isr=false).
Should be called periodically (e.g., in the main loop) to service the Type-C/PD stack.
Underlying ports should be initialized with tuc_init for meaningful processing.

functions.name: tcd_int_handler
functions.signature: void tcd_int_handler(uint8_t rhport);
functions.description: Interrupt handler entry for the TinyUSB Type-C Driver (TCD). This is also aliased as tuc_int_handler. It should be invoked by the MCU’s interrupt vector when the Type-C/PD hardware triggers an interrupt for the given port.
requirements: Must be called in interrupt context by the platform’s interrupt vector for the corresponding Type-C/PD hardware.
rhport must identify the port that generated the interrupt and be a valid port index.
The Type-C stack for the given rhport should be initialized (tuc_init) before interrupts are enabled for that port.

functions.name: tuc_pd_data_received_cb
functions.signature: bool tuc_pd_data_received_cb(uint8_t rhport, pd_header_t const* header, uint8_t const* dobj, uint8_t const* p_end);
functions.description: Application callback invoked by the stack when a USB Power Delivery message with data objects is received on a port. header describes the PD message; dobj points to the first byte of the data objects; p_end points one past the last valid byte. Returns a boolean status (exact semantics not documented here). This function is expected to be implemented by the application.
requirements: This is an application-implemented callback; the stack calls it—do not call it directly unless testing your own implementation.
When implementing, treat header as a valid, non-null pointer to a received PD header.

When implementing, dobj points to a contiguous byte buffer containing PD data objects; p_end points to the end of that buffer (one past the last byte). The range [dobj, p_end) must be respected when reading.
Implementation must not dereference header, dobj, or p_end if they are NULL; be defensive as exact NULLability is not documented.
Return value semantics are not documented; if used, document behavior in your application (unknown).

import random
from typing import List

# Generator for arbitrary binary data used by the fuzzing stubs.
# Goals based on stubs:
# - Provide non-empty strings for FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to fill buffers.
# - Provide varied lengths, often reused to size src/dest buffers, queue payloads, and opaque defs.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Include a mix of printable and non-printable bytes to exercise copying/aggregation paths.
# - Include repeated patterns and structured segments so multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls can
#   draw different slices while still being valid arbitrary data.

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"TinyUSB", b"queue", b"mutex", b"semaphore", b"endpoint", b"device",
    b"host", b"descriptor", b"control", b"bulk", b"interrupt", b"iso",
    b"DFU", b"BOS", b"string", b"USB2.0", b"HS", b"FS", b"IAD", b"VIDPID"
]

HEX_CHARS = b"0123456789ABCDEF"


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _pattern_block(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a block combining several subpatterns to be robust as arbitrary data.
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Repeating byte runs (0x00, 0xFF, and random)
    for b in (0x00, 0xFF, rng.randrange(0, 256)):
        run_len = rng.randrange(8, 64)
        parts.append(bytes([b]) * run_len)

    # 2) Incrementing/decrementing sequences
    inc_len = rng.randrange(16, 96)
    start = rng.randrange(0, 256)
    parts.append(bytes((start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(inc_len)))

    dec_len = rng.randrange(16, 96)
    start = rng.randrange(0, 256)
    parts.append(bytes((start - i) & 0xFF for i in range(dec_len)))

    # 3) ASCII words separated by punctuation and NULs
    word_count = rng.randrange(3, 10)
    for _ in range(word_count):
        w = rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS)
        sep = bytes([rng.choice([0x00, 0x20, 0x2C, 0x3B, 0x0A, 0x09])])
        parts.append(w + sep)

    # 4) Hex-like segments often useful as readable payloads
    hex_len = rng.randrange(16, 128)
    hex_bytes = bytearray()
    for _ in range(hex_len):
        hex_bytes.append(rng.choice(HEX_CHARS))
    parts.append(bytes(hex_bytes))

    # 5) Random block
    parts.append(_rand_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(64, 256)))

    # 6) Short diverse prefixes/suffixes (little-endian numbers)
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(2, 6)):
        v = rng.getrandbits(32)
        parts.append(v.to_bytes(4, 'little'))

    block = b"".join(parts)
    if len(block) > max_len:
        block = block[:max_len]
    return block


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide overall size, keep <= 4096. Favor mid-to-large to satisfy multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR uses.
    total_size = rng.randrange(512, 2048)

    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Compose multiple varied blocks to increase diversity across FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    remaining = total_size
    while remaining > 0:
        # Each block up to 512 bytes for variety
        blk_max = min(remaining, rng.randrange(128, 512))
        blk = _pattern_block(rng, blk_max)
        if not blk:
            blk = _rand_bytes(rng, min(remaining, 64))
        chunks.append(blk)
        remaining -= len(blk)

    # Add a small trailer of random length with strong randomness
    trailer_len = rng.randrange(16, 128)
    chunks.append(_rand_bytes(rng, trailer_len))

    data = b"".join(chunks)
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]

    # Ensure non-empty and provide some entropy at both ends
    if len(data) < 64:
        data += _rand_bytes(rng, 64 - len(data))

    return data
